managers.message_to_team: Starting today, every handoff cup needs a handwritten note that connects to that customer—their name, order, or something they told you; a smiley by itself doesn’t count. I’ll check cups during the shift, so please make it part of the handoff every time, even if the line picks up.
managers.private_thought: With the line short and headcount on plan, we can do this without putting the window-time target at much risk, and I don’t want an avoidable audit miss.

managers.message_to_team: When it’s steady like now, put a real note on every handoff cup—name, order, or something they told you, not just a smiley. I’ll check during the shift; when the 7-to-9 rush hits, keep the line moving and skip the note if it’s slowing us down.
managers.private_thought: Mid-morning has enough slack to satisfy the audit, but I’m not trading peak throughput for handwriting on app orders.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate wants a handwritten note on every cup, and I’d love for us to make them feel personal when there’s a natural detail to use—name, order, or something they shared. Please don’t force a conversation when someone’s studying or we’re slammed; let’s keep the connection genuine and help each other out.
managers.private_thought: I don’t want a daily cup check turning a nice idea into one more thing that makes my student partners dread a shift.

managers.message_to_team: Corporate wants a personal note on each cup, so add one when it fits—use their name, order, or something they mentioned. Keep the line moving; I’m not going to check cups today.
managers.private_thought: They barely audit this kiosk, and I have sales to worry about more than chasing notes.

managers.message_to_team: The memo says every handoff cup, so let's make sure each one has a personal note—not just a smiley—and I’ll check cups during the shift. We’re steady today, so please work it into the handoff; if something gets genuinely hectic, tell me and we’ll figure it out.
managers.private_thought: I want to follow this exactly with the district manager watching, but I hope checking every cup doesn’t make the team feel micromanaged.

managers.message_to_team: While the line’s short, put a real note on each cup—use their name, order, or something they said, not just a smiley. If we get a boarding rush, keep the line moving; I’ll check cups when it’s steady again.
managers.private_thought: This is manageable now, but I’m not letting a handwritten note become the reason somebody misses a flight.
